1	# Drain a project end-to-end on composable skills — supervised, not babysat
2	
3	**This is the guiding vision for the drain-cycle project.** It is not a one-off design doc: every decision, project, and ticket aligns to it, and every analytics review or retro is grounded in it. When a project and this doc disagree, change this doc first — deliberately — and let the projects follow. It consolidates the architecture content from `docs/initiative-multi-agent-collaboration.md` (the dispatcher framing) and `agent-skills-shaper/docs/ideas/lifecycle-expansion.md` (the process/workflow split); both are now facets of the single picture here.
4	
5	## 1. Problem
6	
7	I want one toolbox of capabilities that I can use two ways without rebuilding anything:
8	
9	- **By hand** — invoke a single discrete skill at the keyboard when I want exactly that one step (`/shape:design`, `/exec:review`, `/shape:pr-finishing`).
10	- **Unattended** — point an engine at a Linear project and have it run those same skills in the right sequence, ticket by ticket, to a merged reviewable PR — without me watching every step.
11	
12	Today both halves are broken. The skills exist but assume a human is driving; the automation (`drain-cycle`) re-implements the workflow as prompt prose instead of pointing at the skills; and the two have started to diverge. The failure that makes this concrete: a worker can finish the *work* and still not finish the *ticket*, and nothing catches it (§7).
13	
14	The desired end-state: the **same skills** are the unit of work in both modes, and the automation is a thin layer that does what I do by hand as a supervisor — start the work, hold the guardrails, check the result. **The real goal is to replace my own mechanical supervision with an orchestrator** so my attention moves to higher-order work — scoping the next project, validating delivered work, improving the system — instead of watching each ticket run.
15	
16	That autonomy comes at a price I take on deliberately: **automating supervision trades away the live feedback loop.** Supervising by hand, I catch a workflow going wrong early and I pivot fast; an orchestrated run gives that up — it executes to a halt or a Done and I inspect afterward. So I apply autonomy selectively, on work where the trade pays, and I lean on observability to buy back a delayed version of the loop — which is also how I improve the product over time.
17	
18	## 2. Context and constraints
19	
20	**Where this came from.** `drain-cycle` began as "drain a Linear cycle unattended — one ticket, one worker, one diff." Three threads then pulled it forward: the Shaper pack grew an execution half (the `exec:*` skills); a re-scope decision said the pack should *own* the workflow and drain-cycle should shrink to a supervisor (`lifecycle-expansion.md` §2); and a real incident (§7) showed the supervisor trusting the worker too much.
21	
22	**Prior decisions this inherits** (`docs/design-decisions.md`): §1 the spawned agent updates Linear itself; §10 headless workers inherit project config by symlink — *this is what makes a skill behave identically by hand and inside a worker*; §14 halted issues resume by reusing the worktree; §16–18 the Graphite stack-mode + handoff contract. Decision §17 ("`/shape:task` runs inside the worker session") is the high-water mark of the *old* inline-workflow approach and is superseded by the boundary below.
23	
24	**Non-functional requirements** (each with a fitness function — the automated check that keeps it true):
25	
26	| NFR                            | Target                                                                                                                             | Fitness function                                                              |
27	| ------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
28	| Supervisor carries no workflow | 0 workflow-procedure verbs (review/fix/commit/finish sequences) in `drain_cycle/prompt.py`; 0 `gh`/`gt` calls in `orchestrator.py` | `grep` check in the test suite                                                |
29	| Pointer-only prompt            | worker prompt template ≤ 15 lines                                                                                                  | `wc -l` on the template + procedure-verb grep (supervisor project KR3)        |
30	| Recording completeness         | 100% of verify-flow `Done` run-log entries carry an `outcome_verdict`                                                              | `drain-cycle grade` exits non-zero on any violation (correctness project KR2) |
31	| Dual-mode parity               | every execution skill runs to completion both invoked by hand and inside a worker, with no orchestrator-only assumption            | per-skill self-trial on both surfaces (execution project KR1)                 |
32	| End-to-end autonomy            | ≥ 4 of 5 hard tickets reach a merged PR with zero operator fix commits                                                             | `drain-cycle grade` + `git log` post-push-fix scan (correctness project KR1)  |
33	| Reconstructable without watching | every drained ticket answers "what happened and why" after the fact — exit state, halt reason, verdicts, cost, per-step trace — with no live observation needed | run-log entry + OTel `drain.issue` span resolve any ticket's run end-to-end   |
34	
35	## 3. The architecture: two layers, one artifact boundary
36	
37	"Orchestration" was doing two jobs under one word. Split them and the inconsistency dissolves.
38	
39	**Layer 2 — Workflow (the intra-issue layer). Owned by the Shaper pack.**
40	The content-aware sequence of roles inside one ticket: pickup → breakdown → build → review → verify → prepare PR → finish/submit → respond to feedback. It knows the order and the gates. It is already built: `exec:pickup` is the entry skill that delegates each step to its owning skill (`exec:breakdown` / `exec:build` / `exec:review` / `exec:verify` / `exec:finish`). Every step is *also* a skill you can invoke on its own — the sequence is a skill that calls skills, not a monolith.
41	
42	**Layer 1 — Supervision (the session layer). Owned by drain-cycle.**
43	This is the human supervisory role, automated — the mechanical part of what I do when I watch a drain by hand. The content-blind, vendor-agnostic process concerns: spawn a worker session, enforce guardrails (token/turn caps, timeouts), halt on breach, revert Linear state, resume across runs, recover stranded committed work, record the run-log, grade. It never knows what "review" or "verify" *means*. It only asks: *Is the issue Done? Is there an `outcome_verdict`? Does `.drain-handoff.json` carry `pr_urls`?*
44	
45	**The boundary is the artifact.** The two layers never call into each other — they communicate only through durable signals: **Linear state, run-log fields, and the `.drain-handoff.json` handoff file.** The workflow *writes* them; the supervisor *reads* them. That is the entire contract.
46	
47	```
48	                         ┌──────────────── Layer 1: drain-cycle (supervision) ─────────────────┐
49	   manual mode           │  spawn · guardrails · halt · revert · resume · recover · record ·   │
50	   (you, by hand) ─┐     │  grade        — reads artifacts only, never the workflow's steps    │
51	                   │     └───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┘
52	                   │            reads ▲   writes      │ spawns a worker that runs ▼
53	                   ▼                  │   (run-log,   │
54	        ┌─────────────────────────────│───Linear,────│────────────────────────────────────────┐
55	        │  Layer 2: Shaper pack (workflow)  handoff)  ▼                                         │
56	        │  exec:pickup → breakdown → build → review → verify → prepare → finish → respond       │
57	        │  every box is also a standalone skill you can invoke alone                            │
58	        └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
59	```
60	
61	**The placement test** — for any piece of work, ask: *does this require drain-cycle to know what a role does (Layer 2 → pack), or only whether an artifact exists (Layer 1 → supervisor)?* That single question routes every ticket and prevents the layers from leaking into each other again.
62	
63	**Dual-mode falls out of the split.** Because Layer 2 is just skills and Layer 1 only reads artifacts, the skills carry no dependency on the supervisor. Invoked by hand they do the same thing; driven by a worker they do the same thing. drain-cycle is automation *on top of* the toolbox, never a precondition for it.
64	
65	## 4. Alternatives considered
66	
67	- **Do nothing** — keep the workflow inlined in `prompt.py` and duplicated in the pack. *Blast radius:* the two definitions drift (already happening — the prompt's `/shape:task` directive points at a superseded skill); the §7 failure class persists; no manual reuse of the workflow. *Reversal cost:* cheap today, rising with every divergence.
68	- **Fat supervisor** — drain-cycle inlines all role logic in Python. *Blast radius:* vendor lock-in (only a Claude worker can follow it), no by-hand reuse, every skill change becomes a Python change, prompt bloat. *Reversal cost:* high — unwinding role logic out of the orchestrator.
69	- **No supervisor** — skills self-supervise (each enforces its own caps/halt/resume). *Blast radius:* content-aware code doing process control; can't enforce cross-session token caps or resume after a crash, because a single skill can't see outside its own session. *Reversal cost:* high.
70	- **Recommended: two layers split on the artifact boundary** (§3), skills dual-mode, drain-cycle an optional supervisor. Beats the alternatives on every NFR in §2 and is the only one that delivers both use-modes from one definition.
71	
72	## 5. Recommended approach
73	
74	Adopt the §3 split as the invariant. Concretely:
75	
76	1. **Strip `prompt.py` to a pointer.** The worker prompt becomes "work issue X in worktree Y; follow `exec:pickup`" (≤ 15 lines, no procedure). The workflow lives once, in the pack.
77	2. **Keep the supervisor content-blind.** Its only decisions read artifacts: Done-state, `outcome_verdict`, `pr_urls`. Halting, reverting, resuming, recovering, grading — all keyed off those, never off the workflow's internal steps.
78	3. **Make every execution skill dual-mode by construction.** No skill assumes an orchestrator is present; the supervisor supplies only context (issue, worktree, base) and reads back artifacts.
79	4. **Treat the artifact contract as the API between repos.** Changes to run-log fields / handoff schema are versioned interface changes, reviewed as such.
80	
81	## 6. The verdict-crossing seam (the one piece still unbuilt)
82	
83	The one new integration surface — and a likely one-way door, because it sets the handoff/run-log schema everything downstream reads.
84	
85	Layer 2 produces verdicts: `outcome_verdict` (from `exec:verify`), `prep_verdict` (from `pr-prepare`/`exec:finish`). Layer 1's enforcement and grading need them. But **today `handoff.py` carries only `pr_urls`** — there is no channel for a verdict to cross the boundary back into the run-log. Until there is, the supervisor can recover *unfinished* work (it can see "no `pr_urls`") but cannot act on *rejected* work (it can't see a FAIL verdict), and the grader can't enforce "every Done has a recorded verdict."
86	
87	This seam must be designed before the correctness work proceeds. The decision: **extend the handoff file as the single verdict-carrying artifact** the workflow writes and the supervisor reads — `{pr_urls, outcome_verdict, prep_verdict, ...}` — versus separate channels per verdict. Either way the schema is the contract; pick it deliberately (Open Question 1).
88	
89	## 7. The incident that grounds this: work finished, ticket stranded
90	
91	Cycle `793fc9ea`, issue **ABA-383**: a worker pinned to `model:haiku` committed 4 reviewable slices, then exited *without* running review → `/shape:pr-finishing` → handoff → Done. The supervisor's not-Done halt reverted the issue and **stranded the committed work**. This is the architecture's motivating example: the worker did the Layer-2 work but skipped the finishing steps, and the Layer-1 supervisor — which should enforce completion from the outside — only knew how to halt, not recover. **ABA-393** (orchestrator-enforced completion: a sonnet finishing sub-agent recovers committed-but-unfinished work, opus for fixes) is the Layer-1 answer, and it is pure supervision: it reads "commits exist, but not Done / no `pr_urls`" and acts, never touching what the workflow means.
92	
93	## 8. How the projects map onto this design
94	
95	| Linear project                                         | Layer    | Status      | What it is under this design                                                                                                                                       |
96	| ------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
97	| Issues drain end-to-end on first-party skills          | L2       | Completed   | Built the `exec:*` workflow skills — the reason L2 already exists                                                                                                  |
98	| Consolidate Shaper's Lifecycle into Four Phase Skills  | L2       | In progress | Consolidates the shaping-side skills (idea/project/design/delivery)                                                                                                |
99	| **drain-cycle supervises; the pack owns the workflow** | boundary | Planned     | **Keystone — run first.** Strips `prompt.py` to a pointer, establishes the L1/L2 boundary                                                                          |
100	| Multi-agent collaboration for correctness              | L1       | Backlog     | **Reframe** as the L1 enforcement+recording+grading project (see below)                                                                                            |
101	| Drain past the merge gate                              | L1       | idea        | The supervisor's autonomy horizon: optimistic stacking → trust-tiered auto-merge → resident daemon. All Layer 1 (process), gated behind the boundary landing first |
102	
103	**Reframing "Multi-agent collaboration for correctness."** It predates the boundary, so its six-role *skill-building* is overtaken — those skills now exist in the pack. Split its tickets by the §3 placement test:
104	
105	- **Keep (Layer 1 — supervision not yet built):** recording fields ABA-320/321/322; verifier-gated-Done enforcement ABA-328 + orchestrator recovery ABA-393 (two branches of one post-check — see §6/§7); grading ABA-333/334/336; the one missing Layer-2 skill, PR Responder + the `pr-feedback` subcommand ABA-332 (build the skill into the pack, the subcommand into drain-cycle).
106	- **Close or fold (overtaken — Layer-2 skill-build / worker-wiring that the boundary replaces):** ABA-324/326/327/330.
107	
108	Its KRs survive almost unchanged because they were already phrased as artifact checks ("every Done has a recorded `outcome_verdict`") — Layer-1 by construction. Only the built code had drifted into the worker.
109	
110	## 9. Consequences
111	
112	- **The keystone lands first.** The boundary re-scope — strip `prompt.py`, point at `exec:pickup` — must land before anything else; it is the seam the whole design rests on, and it carries the real integration risk (a pointer-only prompt must drain a real ticket as well as the inlined one did). Everything else is additive once it holds.
113	- **Positive:** one definition serves both use-modes; a non-Claude worker can follow the same prose (vendor-agnostic); ABA-383-class recovery becomes natural Layer-1 behaviour; each layer is independently testable.
114	- **Negative:** the verdict-crossing seam is new surface and a schema one-way door (§6); two repos must stay in sync through the artifact contract, which is now a real interface to version.
115	- **The trade-off is the feedback loop, by design.** Handing supervision to the orchestrator removes the live intervention and rapid pivot that watching a drain by hand gives me. I accept this selectively — on work scoped well enough that the trade pays — and it makes observability essential rather than optional: once I step out of the loop, the run-log, traces, and grade *are* my feedback, delayed and batched (§10). The improvement path is to widen the set of work where the trade pays, which depends directly on how good that observability gets.
116	
117	## 10. Observability is the feedback loop I traded away, bought back
118	
119	Once I step out of the live loop (§9), observability stops being mere operability — it becomes the delayed feedback loop that tells me where a drain went wrong and, run over run, where the product has to improve. It rides the same artifacts that *are* the boundary, so enforcement and inspection are mechanical, not manual. Making it good is what widens the set of work I can safely hand off, so it is a first-class deliverable, not an afterthought:
120	
121	- **Metrics / logs:** the run-log entry per worker exit (exit state, `final_linear_state`, `halt_reason`, the verdict fields once §6 lands) and the OTel `drain.issue` span attributes.
122	- **Fitness functions:** the five NFR checks in §2 — boundary-purity grep, prompt-line cap, `drain-cycle grade` exit code, dual-mode self-trial, end-to-end autonomy scan. These are the alerts; a red fitness function is the signal the design has drifted.
123	- **Rollback:** the keystone re-scope has a defined fallback — if a pointer-only prompt causes 3 consecutive halted drains the inlined prompt would have completed, restore the inline tail and keep the re-scope to guardrails+logging only (the supervisor project's kill condition). ABA-393 recovery is bounded to one attempt per issue per run.
124	- **Failure modes:** worker skips finishing (→ L1 recovery, §7); verdict can't cross (→ §6 blocks correctness work, not the drain itself); restack conflict on merged upstream (→ halt-and-park, per *Drain past the merge gate*).
125	
126	## 11. Open questions
127	
128	1. **How does a verdict cross the boundary? (one-way door)** Does the handoff file become the single verdict-carrying artifact (`{pr_urls, outcome_verdict, prep_verdict, …}`), or do verdicts cross by separate channels? *Owner:* Anton. *Resolution gate:* the keystone re-scope design / the reframed recording milestone — blocks all Layer-1 correctness enforcement.
129	2. **Execution-skill verb namespace.** `exec:*` (current) vs `ship:*` (proposed in `lifecycle-expansion.md`). *Owner:* Anton. *Gate:* before the PR Responder skill is authored.
130	3. **Autonomy host.** Does end-to-end autonomy (Drain past the merge gate) run under a `/loop`/cron relaunch interim, or wait for the resident daemon? *Owner:* Anton. *Gate:* Gear-3 decision, after trust-tiered auto-merge ships.
131	4. **Where dual-mode parity is tested.** What fixture proves a skill behaves identically by hand and inside a worker? *Owner:* Anton. *Gate:* the execution project's fixture harness.
132

Adopt the §3 split as the invariant. Concretely:

1. **Strip `prompt.py` to a pointer.** The worker prompt becomes "work issue X in worktree Y; follow `exec:pickup`" (≤ 15 lines, no procedure). The workflow lives once, in the pack.
2. **Keep the supervisor content-blind.** Its only decisions read artifacts: Done-state, `outcome_verdict`, `pr_urls`. Halting, reverting, resuming, recovering, grading — all keyed off those, never off the workflow's internal steps.
3. **Make every execution skill dual-mode by construction.** No skill assumes an orchestrator is present; the supervisor supplies only context (issue, worktree, base) and reads back artifacts.
4. **Treat the artifact contract as the API between repos.** Changes to run-log fields / handoff schema are versioned interface changes, reviewed as such.

## 6. The verdict-crossing seam (the one piece still unbuilt)

The one new integration surface — and a likely one-way door, because it sets the handoff/run-log schema everything downstream reads.

Layer 2 produces verdicts: `outcome_verdict` (from `exec:verify`), `prep_verdict` (from `pr-prepare`/`exec:finish`). Layer 1's enforcement and grading need them. But **today `handoff.py` carries only `pr_urls`** — there is no channel for a verdict to cross the boundary back into the run-log. Until there is, the supervisor can recover *unfinished* work (it can see "no `pr_urls`") but cannot act on *rejected* work (it can't see a FAIL verdict), and the grader can't enforce "every Done has a recorded verdict."

This seam must be designed before the correctness work proceeds. The decision: **extend the handoff file as the single verdict-carrying artifact** the workflow writes and the supervisor reads — `{pr_urls, outcome_verdict, prep_verdict, ...}` — versus separate channels per verdict. Either way the schema is the contract; pick it deliberately (Open Question 1).

## 7. The incident that grounds this: work finished, ticket stranded

Cycle `793fc9ea`, issue **ABA-383**: a worker pinned to `model:haiku` committed 4 reviewable slices, then exited *without* running review → `/shape:pr-finishing` → handoff → Done. The supervisor's not-Done halt reverted the issue and **stranded the committed work**. This is the architecture's motivating example: the worker did the Layer-2 work but skipped the finishing steps, and the Layer-1 supervisor — which should enforce completion from the outside — only knew how to halt, not recover. **ABA-393** (orchestrator-enforced completion: a sonnet finishing sub-agent recovers committed-but-unfinished work, opus for fixes) is the Layer-1 answer, and it is pure supervision: it reads "commits exist, but not Done / no `pr_urls`" and acts, never touching what the workflow means.

## 8. How the projects map onto this design

| Linear project                                         | Layer    | Status      | What it is under this design                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Issues drain end-to-end on first-party skills          | L2       | Completed   | Built the `exec:*` workflow skills — the reason L2 already exists                                                                                                  |
| Consolidate Shaper's Lifecycle into Four Phase Skills  | L2       | In progress | Consolidates the shaping-side skills (idea/project/design/delivery)                                                                                                |
| **drain-cycle supervises; the pack owns the workflow** | boundary | Planned     | **Keystone — run first.** Strips `prompt.py` to a pointer, establishes the L1/L2 boundary                                                                          |
| Multi-agent collaboration for correctness              | L1       | Backlog     | **Reframe** as the L1 enforcement+recording+grading project (see below)                                                                                            |
| Drain past the merge gate                              | L1       | idea        | The supervisor's autonomy horizon: optimistic stacking → trust-tiered auto-merge → resident daemon. All Layer 1 (process), gated behind the boundary landing first |

**Reframing "Multi-agent collaboration for correctness."** It predates the boundary, so its six-role *skill-building* is overtaken — those skills now exist in the pack. Split its tickets by the §3 placement test:

- **Keep (Layer 1 — supervision not yet built):** recording fields ABA-320/321/322; verifier-gated-Done enforcement ABA-328 + orchestrator recovery ABA-393 (two branches of one post-check — see §6/§7); grading ABA-333/334/336; the one missing Layer-2 skill, PR Responder + the `pr-feedback` subcommand ABA-332 (build the skill into the pack, the subcommand into drain-cycle).
- **Close or fold (overtaken — Layer-2 skill-build / worker-wiring that the boundary replaces):** ABA-324/326/327/330.

Its KRs survive almost unchanged because they were already phrased as artifact checks ("every Done has a recorded `outcome_verdict`") — Layer-1 by construction. Only the built code had drifted into the worker.

## 9. Consequences

- **The keystone lands first.** The boundary re-scope — strip `prompt.py`, point at `exec:pickup` — must land before anything else; it is the seam the whole design rests on, and it carries the real integration risk (a pointer-only prompt must drain a real ticket as well as the inlined one did). Everything else is additive once it holds.
- **Positive:** one definition serves both use-modes; a non-Claude worker can follow the same prose (vendor-agnostic); ABA-383-class recovery becomes natural Layer-1 behaviour; each layer is independently testable.
- **Negative:** the verdict-crossing seam is new surface and a schema one-way door (§6); two repos must stay in sync through the artifact contract, which is now a real interface to version.
- **The trade-off is the feedback loop, by design.** Handing supervision to the orchestrator removes the live intervention and rapid pivot that watching a drain by hand gives me. I accept this selectively — on work scoped well enough that the trade pays — and it makes observability essential rather than optional: once I step out of the loop, the run-log, traces, and grade *are* my feedback, delayed and batched (§10). The improvement path is to widen the set of work where the trade pays, which depends directly on how good that observability gets.

## 10. Observability is the feedback loop I traded away, bought back

Once I step out of the live loop (§9), observability stops being mere operability — it becomes the delayed feedback loop that tells me where a drain went wrong and, run over run, where the product has to improve. It rides the same artifacts that *are* the boundary, so enforcement and inspection are mechanical, not manual. Making it good is what widens the set of work I can safely hand off, so it is a first-class deliverable, not an afterthought:

- **Metrics / logs:** the run-log entry per worker exit (exit state, `final_linear_state`, `halt_reason`, the verdict fields once §6 lands) and the OTel `drain.issue` span attributes.
- **Fitness functions:** the five NFR checks in §2 — boundary-purity grep, prompt-line cap, `drain-cycle grade` exit code, dual-mode self-trial, end-to-end autonomy scan. These are the alerts; a red fitness function is the signal the design has drifted.
- **Rollback:** the keystone re-scope has a defined fallback — if a pointer-only prompt causes 3 consecutive halted drains the inlined prompt would have completed, restore the inline tail and keep the re-scope to guardrails+logging only (the supervisor project's kill condition). ABA-393 recovery is bounded to one attempt per issue per run.
- **Failure modes:** worker skips finishing (→ L1 recovery, §7); verdict can't cross (→ §6 blocks correctness work, not the drain itself); restack conflict on merged upstream (→ halt-and-park, per *Drain past the merge gate*).

## 11. Open questions

1. **How does a verdict cross the boundary? (one-way door)** Does the handoff file become the single verdict-carrying artifact (`{pr_urls, outcome_verdict, prep_verdict, …}`), or do verdicts cross by separate channels? *Owner:* Anton. *Resolution gate:* the keystone re-scope design / the reframed recording milestone — blocks all Layer-1 correctness enforcement.
2. **Execution-skill verb namespace.** `exec:*` (current) vs `ship:*` (proposed in `lifecycle-expansion.md`). *Owner:* Anton. *Gate:* before the PR Responder skill is authored.
3. **Autonomy host.** Does end-to-end autonomy (Drain past the merge gate) run under a `/loop`/cron relaunch interim, or wait for the resident daemon? *Owner:* Anton. *Gate:* Gear-3 decision, after trust-tiered auto-merge ships.
4. **Where dual-mode parity is tested.** What fixture proves a skill behaves identically by hand and inside a worker? *Owner:* Anton. *Gate:* the execution project's fixture harness.

1	# Linear initiative — multi-agent collaboration for correctness
2	
3	> **Now a facet of the north-star.** The system architecture this initiative assumed is consolidated in [`docs/designs/end-to-end-skill-drain.md`](designs/end-to-end-skill-drain.md). Under that design this initiative is reframed as the **Layer-1 (supervision) enforcement + recording + grading** project — its six-role *skill-building* is overtaken by the pack's `exec:*` skills. Read the north-star first; treat the role/flow detail below as historical context for the recording/enforcement/grading work that survives.
4	
5	**Six agent-driven roles take a Linear ticket from intake to merged PR — so hard tickets don't silently ship with missing AC.**
6	
7	**The bet.** drain-cycle today drains a Linear cycle unattended — one ticket, one worker, one diff. The next step: six agent-driven roles operating end-to-end on the same ticket — task-shaping before code, outcome verification before Done, structured PR preparation, and autonomous handling of human review feedback. Same operator, same tickets, less manual shepherding.
8	
9	**What we'll know in 5 hard tickets.** Of the next 5 hard tickets drained under the new flow, the bet is ≥ 3 ship and merge with no operator-pushed fix commits. Otherwise the kill condition triggers (§5) and contract enforcement reverts.
10	
11	---
12	
13	## 1 The problem and the bet
14	
15	**Why this matters beyond drain-cycle.** drain-cycle is the batch driver for a growing toolbox of composable skills and MCPs. Each new skill compounds across both modes of use — at the keyboard during interactive work, and inside a worker session during a drain. This initiative ships the next four skills plus two CLI subcommands the toolbox needs to take a hard Linear ticket from intake to a merged PR, plus the durable contracts (run-log fields, Linear-issue dual-write, OTel attrs) that make their outputs inspectable afterwards.
16	
17	drain-cycle evolves from "drain a Linear cycle unattended" toward a **UNIX-philosophy dispatcher for composable skill primitives** — Linear tickets as the work queue, skills+MCPs as the small tools, and `drain-cycle` itself as the batch-mode shell that composes them. The operator (you) drives the *why* (initiative goal + KRs) and the *what* (outcome-focused Linear issue); agents handle the *how* through a defined set of skills. The same skills run manually at the keyboard or automatically inside a worker session — design decision §10's symlink makes this true.
18	
19	The operator failure mode this initiative addresses: **complex tickets that can't be sliced further** where the worker forgets details, under-verifies, or submits an unstructured PR — followed by human review comments piling up while the operator manually re-invokes the agent each round. Three concrete failures today:
20	
21	1. **Silent Done on hard tickets.** Complex unsliceable tickets get drained; the worker self-asserts Done; the diff misses AC; the operator finds out at PR review and fixes by hand. *(e.g., a ticket asks for "halt the drain if Linear label resolution returns ambiguous matches"; the worker ships the label-parse change but never adds the halt logic; the diff passes self-review because nothing it touches asserts the halt-on-ambiguity contract.)* Left unaddressed, the unattended-drain promise breaks on the tickets where it matters most.
22	2. **Unstructured PR submission.** PRs land without What/Why/Focus guidance; the reviewer has to guess what to look at, or the operator manually rewrites the body. *(e.g., a multi-file refactor lands with a subject line and no body; the reviewer reads the diff blind to find out whether the risky bit is in `labels.py` or `worker.py`.)* Left unaddressed, PR review burden stays entirely on the human — auto-mergeable changes get the same scrutiny as risky ones, and review throughput suffers.
23	3. **Stalled feedback loops.** Human review comments accumulate on stacked PRs; the operator manually re-invokes claude each round. *(e.g., a stacked PR gets three rounds of review comments across two days; each round the operator opens the worktree, re-launches claude, and shepherds the fix manually.)* Left unaddressed, the agent ecosystem stops at code-submission time instead of running end-to-end through merge.
24	
25	The bet: six agent-driven roles end-to-end, each backed by a skill (or CLI subcommand) fitting the UNIX-philosophy frame. A drained ticket flows through the pipeline below; the per-role detail table follows.
26	
27	```
28	┌─ Operator (you) ──────────────────────────────────────────┐
29	│  throughout · defines why (KRs) + what (Linear ticket)    │
30	└──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
31	                               ▼
32	┌─ Task Shaper ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
33	│  before code · /shape:task                                │
34	│  → enriched AC + sizing decision + per-stack task list    │
35	└──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
36	                               ▼
37	┌─ Implementer ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
38	│  middle · 6 existing build/test/review/commit skills      │
39	│  → code + tests + in-session code review                  │
40	└──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
41	                               ▼
42	┌─ Outcome Verifier ────────────────────────────────────────┐
43	│  after impl · /shape:verify-implementation                │
44	│  → pass/fail verdict in run log (gates Done)              │
45	└──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
46	                               ▼
47	┌─ PR Preparer ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
48	│  before submit · /shape:pr-prepare                        │
49	│  → What/Why/Focus body OR auto-merge label                │
50	└──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
51	                               ▼
52	┌─ PR Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────┐
53	│  on review feedback · /shape:pr-respond                   │
54	│  (operator launches via `drain-cycle pr-feedback`)        │
55	│  → fix lands on stack · comment IDs tracked               │
56	└──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
57	                               ▼
58	┌─ Grader ──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
59	│  post-drain · `drain-cycle grade-draft <issue>`           │
60	│  → ~/.drain-cycle/grades/<issue>.md                       │
61	│    (status: draft → operator confirms)                    │
62	└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
63	```
64	
65	| # | Role | Phase | Skill / CLI | Status |
66	|---|---|---|---|---|
67	| 0 | **Operator** (you) | Throughout | Operator-side skill table; defines *why* + *what* | — |
68	| 1 | **Task Shaper** | Before code | `/shape:task` *(complements `/shape:planning-and-task-breakdown`)* | [R] |
69	| 2 | **Implementer** | Middle | 6 existing skills (incremental-implementation, test-driven-development, source-driven-development, code-review-and-quality, git-workflow-and-versioning, debugging-and-error-recovery) | [E] |
70	| 3 | **Outcome Verifier** | After implementation, before Done | `/shape:verify-implementation` *(new)* | [N] |
71	| 4 | **PR Preparer** | After Outcome Verifier passes, before PR submission | `/shape:pr-prepare` *(new)* | [N] |
72	| 5 | **PR Responder** | On new human review comments (operator-launched polling loop) | `/shape:pr-respond` *(new)*, launched via `drain-cycle pr-feedback` subcommand | [N] |
73	| 6 | **Grader** (post-drain) | After worker session finishes | `drain-cycle grade-draft <issue>` CLI subcommand | [—] |
74	
75	Roles 1 and 3 are a **complementary pair**: `/shape:task` defines the outcome-shaped task list at the start; `/shape:verify-implementation` validates the outcome at the end. Roles 4 and 5 are the **PR-side pair**: Preparer shapes outbound PRs, Responder addresses inbound review feedback. Role 6 is operator-confirm scaffolding for grading the initiative against its KRs.
76	
77	**If the initiative is built:**
78	
79	- **Hard tickets clear AC before they land.** The Outcome Verifier sees the diff before Done is recorded; the verdict goes to the run log; halt-on-fail leaves the worktree intact for operator inspection rather than producing a silent partial.
80	- **PR review starts with a structured map.** Reviewers open a PR and see What / Why / Focus from the start; auto-mergeable changes route past human review correctly; risky changes get the human attention they earn. Review throughput rises because reviewers no longer parse intent from the diff alone.
81	- **Human review feedback closes its own loop.** The operator launches `drain-cycle pr-feedback`; new review comments get addressed on the right stack node; comment IDs are tracked to prevent double-handling; the loop continues until the operator stops it. The agent ecosystem runs end-to-end through merge rather than stopping at submit-time.
82	
83	**Constraints:**
84	
85	- Subscription auth only (Claude Code / Codex CLI subprocess) — no API-key models. GitHub webhooks are free, but the agent can't run inside GitHub Actions; agent work happens on the operator's machine.
86	- Correctness > throughput. No parallel drains. No throughput-focused changes.
87	
88	## 2 Affected repos
89	
90	- **`drain-cycle`** — primary. Worker integration of roles 1–5, run-log schema extensions, `verify` label mechanism, CLI subcommands (`grade-draft`, `grade --flow=verify`), supersession of design decision §1, OTel attribute additions.
91	- **`agent-skills-shaper`** — secondary. Receives one per-ticket task-shaping skill (`/shape:task`, complementing the whole-project `/shape:planning-and-task-breakdown`) and three new skills (`/shape:verify-implementation`, `/shape:pr-prepare`, `/shape:pr-respond`).
92	
93	## 3 Goal and Key results
94	
95	The KRs are plain English — a non-pack-author should grade each in 30 seconds.
96	
97	### 3.0 Goal
98	
99	**For** the operator running drain-cycle on outcome-focused Linear tickets, **we want** six agent-driven roles that take work from ticket to merged PR — task-shaping before code, outcome verification before Done, structured PR preparation, and autonomous response to human review comments — **so that** complex tickets don't silently land with missing AC, PRs are reviewable without guesswork, and human review feedback doesn't create a manual re-invocation tax.
100	
101	### 3.1 KR1 (stretch) — Of the next 5 hard tickets drained with the new flow, ≥ 3 ship and merge with no operator-pushed fix commits *(bet)*
102	
103	- **plain-English version:** when I run drain-cycle on a hard ticket I couldn't break into smaller pieces, six agent roles take it from intake to merged PR. The bet: this catches enough real problems and structures the PRs well enough that most merge cleanly without me pushing fix commits.
104	- **baseline:** 0 of 0 — none of the six roles exist as a connected flow today.
105	- **target:** ≥ 3 of the next 5 hard tickets drained with the new flow ship and merge with no operator-pushed fix commits.
106	- **measured over:** the first 5 hard tickets drained with the new flow (~2 cycles at current cadence).
107	- **how we'll grade it:** per-ticket grade markdown at `~/.drain-cycle/grades/<issue>.md` (auto-drafted by `drain-cycle grade-draft <issue>`, operator confirms `draft` → `confirmed`); `drain-cycle grade --flow=verify` reports the rolled-up pass-rate across the window.
108	
109	### 3.2 KR2 (commit) — Every ticket reaching Done in Linear under the new flow has a recorded Outcome Verifier verdict in the run log; zero exceptions *(brake)*
110	
111	- **plain-English version:** the worker no longer marks its own ticket Done. The contract: a ticket using the new flow reaches Done only if the run log shows the Outcome Verifier ran and produced a verdict. Protects against the failure mode where the agent thinks it's finished but missed half the AC.
112	- **baseline:** silent self-assertion currently possible (per design decision §1); the count of past silent Dones is unknown because the recording fields don't exist yet.
113	- **target:** 0 tickets reach Done in Linear under the new flow without an `outcome_verdict` recorded in the run log.
114	- **measured over:** every cycle running the new flow, for the initiative's duration (cap at 10 cycles if the initiative runs long).
115	- **how we'll grade it:** `drain-cycle grade` fails any entry where `flow == "verify"` AND `final_linear_state == "completed"` AND `outcome_verdict` is absent. Exit code ≠ 0 on any violation. One violation in any cycle fails the KR — this is a brake, not a rate.
116	
117	### 3.3 KR3 (commit) — Every PR submitted under the new flow has the structured What / Why / Focus body, or is correctly routed to auto-merge *(brake)*
118	
119	- **plain-English version:** the PR Preparer either writes a structured What / Why / Focus body and routes the PR for human review, or correctly identifies the PR as auto-mergeable (no critical focus items) and routes it to auto-merge. Either way, every PR ships with a documented routing decision and a reviewable body.
120	- **baseline:** today, PRs from drained tickets carry whatever body the worker produced — typically a one-line subject and no review guidance.
121	- **target:** 0 PRs submitted under the new flow without either (a) structured What/Why/Focus body OR (b) auto-merge label with PR Preparer reasoning attached.
122	- **measured over:** every PR submitted under the new flow, for the initiative's duration.
123	- **how we'll grade it:** PR Preparer writes its decision to a `prep_verdict` field on the run-log entry; `drain-cycle grade` fails any verify-flow entry where `prep_verdict` is absent or where the verdict says "structured body" but the PR body is empty or single-line.
124	
125	The PR Responder (role 5) gets no KR of its own — KR1 captures it structurally (clean-merge rate degrades if the responder doesn't address review feedback).
126	
127	## 4 Appetite
128	
129	**~18–22 issues across five milestones.** Each milestone ends with a review gate — the operator reviews progress and either continues to the next milestone or pauses for a reshape/kill decision if something clear has surfaced. The gate default is review-and-continue, not stop-the-line. Whole-initiative kill conditions are separate (§5).
130	
131	### M1 — Recording infrastructure
132	
133	Build the data layer first, behaviour later.
134	
135	- `verify` Linear label parser added alongside `repo:` / `model:` resolution in `labels.py`.
136	- Run-log schema fields: `flow` (string, e.g. `"verify"`, or `null` for default flow), `outcome_verdict` (object: `{result, findings[], invoked_at}` or `null`), `prep_verdict` (object: `{result, route, reasoning}` or `null`), `responder_runs[]` (array of objects: `{comment_ids[], invoked_at, result}` — appended each time the responder runs).
137	- Matching attributes on the `drain.issue` OTel span.
138	- `docs/design-decisions.md` §1 supersession: write the successor decision explaining the verifier-gated Done contract; mark §1 as superseded.
139	
140	**Gate:** an end-to-end `verify`-labelled ticket drains; new fields populate (all `null` since no roles are wired yet); existing behaviour unchanged.
141	
142	### M2 — Worker-internal loop (Task Shaper, Outcome Verifier, halt path)
143	
144	- **Task Shaper** (`/shape:task`): per-ticket task-shaping skill that takes a Linear issue and produces an enriched AC checklist + sizing decision (single stack vs N stacks) + per-stack task list. Distinct from `/shape:planning-and-task-breakdown` (whole-project / design-doc shaping); the two coexist in the toolbox at different scopes. The precise interface is resolved in design decision §17 (`docs/design-decisions.md`): `/shape:task` runs inside the worker session at implementation time; `/shape:planning-and-task-breakdown` stays at design-doc scope and is not extended to emit per-ticket artefacts.
145	- **Where the sizing decision lands**: dual-write. (a) Fed into the implementer in-session as context; (b) appended to the **Linear issue body** so future resumes / pickups carry the full context without re-running the Task Shaper. The Linear write is the durable artefact.
146	- **Implementer integration**: worker session pulls the Task Shaper output as context; no other implementer changes.
147	- **Outcome Verifier** (`/shape:verify-implementation`): new skill. Inputs: ticket body + Task Shaper output + diff + run-log. Output: structured verdict (pass / fail + findings) written to `outcome_verdict`.
148	- **Halt-on-fail path**: extends decision §8 / §9 machinery — on Outcome Verifier fail, leave worktree, halt cycle, name the breach in `cycle_halt_reason`.
149	
150	**Gate:** 3 verify-labelled hard tickets drained; verdicts recorded; halt path exercised at least once on a deliberate failure (e.g. a synthetic ticket whose AC the implementer can't satisfy).
151	
152	### M3 — PR-shape gate (PR Preparer)
153	
154	- **PR Preparer** (`/shape:pr-prepare`): new skill. Reads stack PRs via Graphite MCP; writes What / Why / Focus body on each; decides auto-merge vs human-review per the carve-out rule (small + no human review needed → auto-merge; otherwise → human-review).
155	- **Auto-merge mechanism**: Graphite-native (`gt submit --merge-when-ready`-equivalent).
156	- Records the decision to `prep_verdict` on the run-log entry.
157	
158	**Gate:** 3 stacks emitted, all with structured What / Why / Focus bodies or auto-merge labels. PR-body assertion in `drain-cycle grade` passes on all three.
159	
160	### M4 — PR-feedback loop (PR Responder)
161	
162	- **PR Responder** (`/shape:pr-respond`): new skill. Reads new review comments on stack PRs via Graphite MCP; makes the fix in the right worktree; pushes to the stack; appends to `responder_runs[]`.
163	- **Trigger model**: a separate operator-launched subcommand — `drain-cycle pr-feedback`. The operator launches it explicitly; the command then runs as a polling loop, addressing PR comments as they arrive, until the operator stops it. Not invoked implicitly at drain-start, not a GitHub Action, not a boot-time background daemon. A foreground polling agent whose lifetime the operator owns.
164	- **Idempotency**: each comment ID tracked in `responder_runs[].comment_ids[]` so the same comment isn't addressed twice across `pr-feedback` invocations.
165	
166	**Gate:** one real PR with operator-left review feedback gets addressed end-to-end by the responder; the fix lands on the stack; the run-log shows the responder run.
167	
168	### M5 — Grading + cost + close-out
169	
170	- **Per-ticket grade template** at `~/.drain-cycle/grades/<issue>.md` with checklist + `status:` field.
171	- **`drain-cycle grade-draft <issue>` CLI subcommand**: one-shot grading prompt. Runs automatically on drain completion (writes `status: draft`); also runs manually for retro-fill on past tickets.
172	- **`drain-cycle grade --flow=verify` subcommand**: reads `confirmed` grade files, reports pass-rate across a ticket window, warns about un-confirmed drafts.
173	- **Silent-Done detection** (KR2 grader): exit nonzero on any `flow == "verify"` AND `final_linear_state == "completed"` AND `outcome_verdict == null` entry.
174	- **Cost-impact handling**: measure per-ticket token multiplier under the new flow; add `verify`-flow-specific overrides in `limits.yml` if cycle cap pressure surfaces.
175	- **Post-launch review**: write a Linear comment on each KR's status at the end of the initiative window; either ship cleanly, pause, or kill.
176	
177	**Gate:** KR grading runs end-to-end; one of {ship cleanly, pause, kill} is decided and recorded.
178	
179	## 5 Kill condition
180	
181	**Primary kill (whole-initiative):** after running the new flow on 5+ hard tickets across 2 cycles, the Outcome Verifier produces zero true-positive findings (every halt was a false positive, and verifier-passed Dones don't visibly improve PR-review outcomes vs default-flow drains).
182	
183	**Secondary concerns (watched at each milestone's review gate, not auto-kills):**
184	
185	- M1 — schema additions break run-log readers or downstream tooling.
186	- M3 — PR Preparer's bodies don't measurably reduce reviewer cognitive load (signal: the operator subjectively prefers the raw worker-produced PRs).
187	- M4 — PR Responder either (a) requires operator intervention to address comments cleanly >50% of the time, or (b) drops or misses comments in practice.
188	
189	Any of these surfacing at a milestone review prompts a discussion (continue / reshape / kill), but the default is continue. Only the primary kill above is automatic.
190	
191	**Action on kill:** revert the contract enforcement (the `verify` label becomes a no-op or is removed); keep the recording fields — they stay in run log + OTel because they're cheap and useful for future investigation; record the negative result as a new decision in `docs/design-decisions.md`.
192	
193	## 6 Out of scope (explicitly)
194	
195	- **Parallel drains.** Decision §8's serial-drain stance unchanged.
196	- **Replacing Graphite.** The PR-side work assumes the Graphite stack flow; switching PR-management tools is a separate decision.
197	- **Multi-operator / multi-tenant workflows.** Single-user product per `AGENTS.md` ("Python, single-user, personal product").

# Linear initiative — multi-agent collaboration for correctness

> **Now a facet of the north-star.** The system architecture this initiative assumed is consolidated in [`docs/designs/end-to-end-skill-drain.md`](designs/end-to-end-skill-drain.md). Under that design this initiative is reframed as the **Layer-1 (supervision) enforcement + recording + grading** project — its six-role *skill-building* is overtaken by the pack's `exec:*` skills. Read the north-star first; treat the role/flow detail below as historical context for the recording/enforcement/grading work that survives.

**Six agent-driven roles take a Linear ticket from intake to merged PR — so hard tickets don't silently ship with missing AC.**

**The bet.** drain-cycle today drains a Linear cycle unattended — one ticket, one worker, one diff. The next step: six agent-driven roles operating end-to-end on the same ticket — task-shaping before code, outcome verification before Done, structured PR preparation, and autonomous handling of human review feedback. Same operator, same tickets, less manual shepherding.

**What we'll know in 5 hard tickets.** Of the next 5 hard tickets drained under the new flow, the bet is ≥ 3 ship and merge with no operator-pushed fix commits. Otherwise the kill condition triggers (§5) and contract enforcement reverts.

---

## 1 The problem and the bet

**Why this matters beyond drain-cycle.** drain-cycle is the batch driver for a growing toolbox of composable skills and MCPs. Each new skill compounds across both modes of use — at the keyboard during interactive work, and inside a worker session during a drain. This initiative ships the next four skills plus two CLI subcommands the toolbox needs to take a hard Linear ticket from intake to a merged PR, plus the durable contracts (run-log fields, Linear-issue dual-write, OTel attrs) that make their outputs inspectable afterwards.

drain-cycle evolves from "drain a Linear cycle unattended" toward a **UNIX-philosophy dispatcher for composable skill primitives** — Linear tickets as the work queue, skills+MCPs as the small tools, and `drain-cycle` itself as the batch-mode shell that composes them. The operator (you) drives the *why* (initiative goal + KRs) and the *what* (outcome-focused Linear issue); agents handle the *how* through a defined set of skills. The same skills run manually at the keyboard or automatically inside a worker session — design decision §10's symlink makes this true.

The operator failure mode this initiative addresses: **complex tickets that can't be sliced further** where the worker forgets details, under-verifies, or submits an unstructured PR — followed by human review comments piling up while the operator manually re-invokes the agent each round. Three concrete failures today:

1. **Silent Done on hard tickets.** Complex unsliceable tickets get drained; the worker self-asserts Done; the diff misses AC; the operator finds out at PR review and fixes by hand. *(e.g., a ticket asks for "halt the drain if Linear label resolution returns ambiguous matches"; the worker ships the label-parse change but never adds the halt logic; the diff passes self-review because nothing it touches asserts the halt-on-ambiguity contract.)* Left unaddressed, the unattended-drain promise breaks on the tickets where it matters most.
2. **Unstructured PR submission.** PRs land without What/Why/Focus guidance; the reviewer has to guess what to look at, or the operator manually rewrites the body. *(e.g., a multi-file refactor lands with a subject line and no body; the reviewer reads the diff blind to find out whether the risky bit is in `labels.py` or `worker.py`.)* Left unaddressed, PR review burden stays entirely on the human — auto-mergeable changes get the same scrutiny as risky ones, and review throughput suffers.
3. **Stalled feedback loops.** Human review comments accumulate on stacked PRs; the operator manually re-invokes claude each round. *(e.g., a stacked PR gets three rounds of review comments across two days; each round the operator opens the worktree, re-launches claude, and shepherds the fix manually.)* Left unaddressed, the agent ecosystem stops at code-submission time instead of running end-to-end through merge.

The bet: six agent-driven roles end-to-end, each backed by a skill (or CLI subcommand) fitting the UNIX-philosophy frame. A drained ticket flows through the pipeline below; the per-role detail table follows.

```
┌─ Operator (you) ──────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  throughout · defines why (KRs) + what (Linear ticket)    │
└──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                               ▼
┌─ Task Shaper ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  before code · /shape:task                                │
│  → enriched AC + sizing decision + per-stack task list    │
└──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                               ▼
┌─ Implementer ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  middle · 6 existing build/test/review/commit skills      │
│  → code + tests + in-session code review                  │
└──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                               ▼
┌─ Outcome Verifier ────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  after impl · /shape:verify-implementation                │
│  → pass/fail verdict in run log (gates Done)              │
└──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                               ▼
┌─ PR Preparer ─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  before submit · /shape:pr-prepare                        │
│  → What/Why/Focus body OR auto-merge label                │
└──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                               ▼
┌─ PR Responder ────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  on review feedback · /shape:pr-respond                   │
│  (operator launches via `drain-cycle pr-feedback`)        │
│  → fix lands on stack · comment IDs tracked               │
└──────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                               ▼
┌─ Grader ──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  post-drain · `drain-cycle grade-draft <issue>`           │
│  → ~/.drain-cycle/grades/<issue>.md                       │
│    (status: draft → operator confirms)                    │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

| # | Role | Phase | Skill / CLI | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | **Operator** (you) | Throughout | Operator-side skill table; defines *why* + *what* | — |
| 1 | **Task Shaper** | Before code | `/shape:task` *(complements `/shape:planning-and-task-breakdown`)* | [R] |
| 2 | **Implementer** | Middle | 6 existing skills (incremental-implementation, test-driven-development, source-driven-development, code-review-and-quality, git-workflow-and-versioning, debugging-and-error-recovery) | [E] |
| 3 | **Outcome Verifier** | After implementation, before Done | `/shape:verify-implementation` *(new)* | [N] |
| 4 | **PR Preparer** | After Outcome Verifier passes, before PR submission | `/shape:pr-prepare` *(new)* | [N] |
| 5 | **PR Responder** | On new human review comments (operator-launched polling loop) | `/shape:pr-respond` *(new)*, launched via `drain-cycle pr-feedback` subcommand | [N] |
| 6 | **Grader** (post-drain) | After worker session finishes | `drain-cycle grade-draft <issue>` CLI subcommand | [—] |

Roles 1 and 3 are a **complementary pair**: `/shape:task` defines the outcome-shaped task list at the start; `/shape:verify-implementation` validates the outcome at the end. Roles 4 and 5 are the **PR-side pair**: Preparer shapes outbound PRs, Responder addresses inbound review feedback. Role 6 is operator-confirm scaffolding for grading the initiative against its KRs.

**If the initiative is built:**

- **Hard tickets clear AC before they land.** The Outcome Verifier sees the diff before Done is recorded; the verdict goes to the run log; halt-on-fail leaves the worktree intact for operator inspection rather than producing a silent partial.
- **PR review starts with a structured map.** Reviewers open a PR and see What / Why / Focus from the start; auto-mergeable changes route past human review correctly; risky changes get the human attention they earn. Review throughput rises because reviewers no longer parse intent from the diff alone.
- **Human review feedback closes its own loop.** The operator launches `drain-cycle pr-feedback`; new review comments get addressed on the right stack node; comment IDs are tracked to prevent double-handling; the loop continues until the operator stops it. The agent ecosystem runs end-to-end through merge rather than stopping at submit-time.

**Constraints:**

- Subscription auth only (Claude Code / Codex CLI subprocess) — no API-key models. GitHub webhooks are free, but the agent can't run inside GitHub Actions; agent work happens on the operator's machine.
- Correctness > throughput. No parallel drains. No throughput-focused changes.

## 2 Affected repos

- **`drain-cycle`** — primary. Worker integration of roles 1–5, run-log schema extensions, `verify` label mechanism, CLI subcommands (`grade-draft`, `grade --flow=verify`), supersession of design decision §1, OTel attribute additions.
- **`agent-skills-shaper`** — secondary. Receives one per-ticket task-shaping skill (`/shape:task`, complementing the whole-project `/shape:planning-and-task-breakdown`) and three new skills (`/shape:verify-implementation`, `/shape:pr-prepare`, `/shape:pr-respond`).

## 3 Goal and Key results

The KRs are plain English — a non-pack-author should grade each in 30 seconds.

### 3.0 Goal

**For** the operator running drain-cycle on outcome-focused Linear tickets, **we want** six agent-driven roles that take work from ticket to merged PR — task-shaping before code, outcome verification before Done, structured PR preparation, and autonomous response to human review comments — **so that** complex tickets don't silently land with missing AC, PRs are reviewable without guesswork, and human review feedback doesn't create a manual re-invocation tax.

### 3.1 KR1 (stretch) — Of the next 5 hard tickets drained with the new flow, ≥ 3 ship and merge with no operator-pushed fix commits *(bet)*

- **plain-English version:** when I run drain-cycle on a hard ticket I couldn't break into smaller pieces, six agent roles take it from intake to merged PR. The bet: this catches enough real problems and structures the PRs well enough that most merge cleanly without me pushing fix commits.
- **baseline:** 0 of 0 — none of the six roles exist as a connected flow today.
- **target:** ≥ 3 of the next 5 hard tickets drained with the new flow ship and merge with no operator-pushed fix commits.
- **measured over:** the first 5 hard tickets drained with the new flow (~2 cycles at current cadence).
- **how we'll grade it:** per-ticket grade markdown at `~/.drain-cycle/grades/<issue>.md` (auto-drafted by `drain-cycle grade-draft <issue>`, operator confirms `draft` → `confirmed`); `drain-cycle grade --flow=verify` reports the rolled-up pass-rate across the window.

### 3.2 KR2 (commit) — Every ticket reaching Done in Linear under the new flow has a recorded Outcome Verifier verdict in the run log; zero exceptions *(brake)*

- **plain-English version:** the worker no longer marks its own ticket Done. The contract: a ticket using the new flow reaches Done only if the run log shows the Outcome Verifier ran and produced a verdict. Protects against the failure mode where the agent thinks it's finished but missed half the AC.
- **baseline:** silent self-assertion currently possible (per design decision §1); the count of past silent Dones is unknown because the recording fields don't exist yet.
- **target:** 0 tickets reach Done in Linear under the new flow without an `outcome_verdict` recorded in the run log.
- **measured over:** every cycle running the new flow, for the initiative's duration (cap at 10 cycles if the initiative runs long).
- **how we'll grade it:** `drain-cycle grade` fails any entry where `flow == "verify"` AND `final_linear_state == "completed"` AND `outcome_verdict` is absent. Exit code ≠ 0 on any violation. One violation in any cycle fails the KR — this is a brake, not a rate.

### 3.3 KR3 (commit) — Every PR submitted under the new flow has the structured What / Why / Focus body, or is correctly routed to auto-merge *(brake)*

- **plain-English version:** the PR Preparer either writes a structured What / Why / Focus body and routes the PR for human review, or correctly identifies the PR as auto-mergeable (no critical focus items) and routes it to auto-merge. Either way, every PR ships with a documented routing decision and a reviewable body.
- **baseline:** today, PRs from drained tickets carry whatever body the worker produced — typically a one-line subject and no review guidance.
- **target:** 0 PRs submitted under the new flow without either (a) structured What/Why/Focus body OR (b) auto-merge label with PR Preparer reasoning attached.
- **measured over:** every PR submitted under the new flow, for the initiative's duration.
- **how we'll grade it:** PR Preparer writes its decision to a `prep_verdict` field on the run-log entry; `drain-cycle grade` fails any verify-flow entry where `prep_verdict` is absent or where the verdict says "structured body" but the PR body is empty or single-line.

The PR Responder (role 5) gets no KR of its own — KR1 captures it structurally (clean-merge rate degrades if the responder doesn't address review feedback).

## 4 Appetite

**~18–22 issues across five milestones.** Each milestone ends with a review gate — the operator reviews progress and either continues to the next milestone or pauses for a reshape/kill decision if something clear has surfaced. The gate default is review-and-continue, not stop-the-line. Whole-initiative kill conditions are separate (§5).

### M1 — Recording infrastructure

Build the data layer first, behaviour later.

- `verify` Linear label parser added alongside `repo:` / `model:` resolution in `labels.py`.
- Run-log schema fields: `flow` (string, e.g. `"verify"`, or `null` for default flow), `outcome_verdict` (object: `{result, findings[], invoked_at}` or `null`), `prep_verdict` (object: `{result, route, reasoning}` or `null`), `responder_runs[]` (array of objects: `{comment_ids[], invoked_at, result}` — appended each time the responder runs).
- Matching attributes on the `drain.issue` OTel span.
- `docs/design-decisions.md` §1 supersession: write the successor decision explaining the verifier-gated Done contract; mark §1 as superseded.

**Gate:** an end-to-end `verify`-labelled ticket drains; new fields populate (all `null` since no roles are wired yet); existing behaviour unchanged.

### M2 — Worker-internal loop (Task Shaper, Outcome Verifier, halt path)

- **Task Shaper** (`/shape:task`): per-ticket task-shaping skill that takes a Linear issue and produces an enriched AC checklist + sizing decision (single stack vs N stacks) + per-stack task list. Distinct from `/shape:planning-and-task-breakdown` (whole-project / design-doc shaping); the two coexist in the toolbox at different scopes. The precise interface is resolved in design decision §17 (`docs/design-decisions.md`): `/shape:task` runs inside the worker session at implementation time; `/shape:planning-and-task-breakdown` stays at design-doc scope and is not extended to emit per-ticket artefacts.
- **Where the sizing decision lands**: dual-write. (a) Fed into the implementer in-session as context; (b) appended to the **Linear issue body** so future resumes / pickups carry the full context without re-running the Task Shaper. The Linear write is the durable artefact.
- **Implementer integration**: worker session pulls the Task Shaper output as context; no other implementer changes.
- **Outcome Verifier** (`/shape:verify-implementation`): new skill. Inputs: ticket body + Task Shaper output + diff + run-log. Output: structured verdict (pass / fail + findings) written to `outcome_verdict`.
- **Halt-on-fail path**: extends decision §8 / §9 machinery — on Outcome Verifier fail, leave worktree, halt cycle, name the breach in `cycle_halt_reason`.

**Gate:** 3 verify-labelled hard tickets drained; verdicts recorded; halt path exercised at least once on a deliberate failure (e.g. a synthetic ticket whose AC the implementer can't satisfy).

### M3 — PR-shape gate (PR Preparer)

- **PR Preparer** (`/shape:pr-prepare`): new skill. Reads stack PRs via Graphite MCP; writes What / Why / Focus body on each; decides auto-merge vs human-review per the carve-out rule (small + no human review needed → auto-merge; otherwise → human-review).
- **Auto-merge mechanism**: Graphite-native (`gt submit --merge-when-ready`-equivalent).
- Records the decision to `prep_verdict` on the run-log entry.

**Gate:** 3 stacks emitted, all with structured What / Why / Focus bodies or auto-merge labels. PR-body assertion in `drain-cycle grade` passes on all three.

### M4 — PR-feedback loop (PR Responder)

- **PR Responder** (`/shape:pr-respond`): new skill. Reads new review comments on stack PRs via Graphite MCP; makes the fix in the right worktree; pushes to the stack; appends to `responder_runs[]`.
- **Trigger model**: a separate operator-launched subcommand — `drain-cycle pr-feedback`. The operator launches it explicitly; the command then runs as a polling loop, addressing PR comments as they arrive, until the operator stops it. Not invoked implicitly at drain-start, not a GitHub Action, not a boot-time background daemon. A foreground polling agent whose lifetime the operator owns.
- **Idempotency**: each comment ID tracked in `responder_runs[].comment_ids[]` so the same comment isn't addressed twice across `pr-feedback` invocations.

**Gate:** one real PR with operator-left review feedback gets addressed end-to-end by the responder; the fix lands on the stack; the run-log shows the responder run.

### M5 — Grading + cost + close-out

- **Per-ticket grade template** at `~/.drain-cycle/grades/<issue>.md` with checklist + `status:` field.
- **`drain-cycle grade-draft <issue>` CLI subcommand**: one-shot grading prompt. Runs automatically on drain completion (writes `status: draft`); also runs manually for retro-fill on past tickets.
- **`drain-cycle grade --flow=verify` subcommand**: reads `confirmed` grade files, reports pass-rate across a ticket window, warns about un-confirmed drafts.
- **Silent-Done detection** (KR2 grader): exit nonzero on any `flow == "verify"` AND `final_linear_state == "completed"` AND `outcome_verdict == null` entry.
- **Cost-impact handling**: measure per-ticket token multiplier under the new flow; add `verify`-flow-specific overrides in `limits.yml` if cycle cap pressure surfaces.
- **Post-launch review**: write a Linear comment on each KR's status at the end of the initiative window; either ship cleanly, pause, or kill.

**Gate:** KR grading runs end-to-end; one of {ship cleanly, pause, kill} is decided and recorded.

## 5 Kill condition

**Primary kill (whole-initiative):** after running the new flow on 5+ hard tickets across 2 cycles, the Outcome Verifier produces zero true-positive findings (every halt was a false positive, and verifier-passed Dones don't visibly improve PR-review outcomes vs default-flow drains).

**Secondary concerns (watched at each milestone's review gate, not auto-kills):**

- M1 — schema additions break run-log readers or downstream tooling.
- M3 — PR Preparer's bodies don't measurably reduce reviewer cognitive load (signal: the operator subjectively prefers the raw worker-produced PRs).
- M4 — PR Responder either (a) requires operator intervention to address comments cleanly >50% of the time, or (b) drops or misses comments in practice.

Any of these surfacing at a milestone review prompts a discussion (continue / reshape / kill), but the default is continue. Only the primary kill above is automatic.

**Action on kill:** revert the contract enforcement (the `verify` label becomes a no-op or is removed); keep the recording fields — they stay in run log + OTel because they're cheap and useful for future investigation; record the negative result as a new decision in `docs/design-decisions.md`.

## 6 Out of scope (explicitly)

- **Parallel drains.** Decision §8's serial-drain stance unchanged.
- **Replacing Graphite.** The PR-side work assumes the Graphite stack flow; switching PR-management tools is a separate decision.
- **Multi-operator / multi-tenant workflows.** Single-user product per `AGENTS.md` ("Python, single-user, personal product").

content.text: The vision doc and initiative doc are current. Now let me assess the older docs — the `tasks/`, `ideas/`, and the possibly-duplicated integration-test docs. I'll dispatch an Explore agent to characterize each against the vision so I can make discard/keep/realign calls.

content.text:
Perfect. Now I have enough information. Let me compile the inventory report.

## Inventory Report

**docs/tasks/multi-agent-collaboration.md**
(a) A comprehensive task plan for an autonomous "multi-agent collaboration" initiative covering 18 tasks in five phases (M1–M5), spanning recording infrastructure, worker-internal loop, PR-shape gate, PR-feedback loop, and grading. Written 2026-05-28.
(b) **References current architecture** — explicitly names the two-layer structure ("Layer 1 supervision / Layer 2 workflow"), mentions exec:* skills (`/shape:task`, `/shape:verify-implementation`, `/shape:pr-prepare`, `/shape:pr-respond`), and defines the artifact boundary (run-log, grade files, Linear issue bodies as durable surfaces).
(c) **Not superseded**; unique scope covering the full initiative pipeline for verify-flow grading and KR1/2/3 automation.
(d) No staleness markers; all tasks forward-looking with open questions and kill-condition gates.

---

**docs/tasks/rerun-after-halt-detect-cleanly.md**
(a) An older task plan (last updated 2026-05-22) for detecting and cleanly reporting leftover worktrees on re-run by raising a `PriorArtefactsExist` exception.
(b) **Explicitly superseded** — the file carries a supersession note at the top pointing to `docs/design-decisions.md` §14 (halted issues resume on re-run). The shipped design (worktree reuse via `worktree.ensure`) eliminates the friction this doc was written to address.
(c) **Superseded by design-decisions.md §14**; kept for design history.
(d) Marked "do not act on the task list below"; clear staleness signal.

---

**docs/tasks/us-a-unattended-cycle-drain.md**
(a) The foundational task plan for US-A (unattended cycle drain), last updated 2026-05-21, containing 7 tasks for orchestrator bootstrap, sorting, iteration, prompt templating, halt-on-not-Done, and acceptance validation.
(b) **References pre-architecture design** — points to `README.md` (not the two-layer vision doc), no mention of exec:* skills or Layer 1/2 split. This is the base orchestrator skeleton before the multi-agent / verify-flow initiative.
(c) **Not superseded individually**; completed and integrated into the full pipeline. Task 7 (In Progress transition) is an amendment surfaced post-acceptance (ABA-209).
(d) No staleness; tasks shipped and marked Done.

---

**docs/tasks/us-b-halt-i-can-inspect.md**
(a) The task plan for US-B (halt I can inspect), last updated 2026-05-22, specifying halt-message formatting, run-log halt entries, and acceptance validation. Three tasks, two shipped (Task 1, Task 2 marked DONE 2026-05-22), one completed with live smoke (Task 3).
(b) **References pre-architecture design** — like US-A, pins design to README, no mention of verify-flow or Layer 1/2. This is halt UX on top of the base orchestrator.
(c) **Not superseded**; foundational piece that later tasks (US-C through D and the multi-agent initiative) build on.
(d) Minimal staleness; all tasks DONE or shipped, live smoke documented.

---

**docs/tasks/us-c-artefacts-that-grade-the-krs.md**
(a) The task plan for US-C (artefacts that grade the KRs), last updated 2026-05-22 (with schema amendment: `time_spent` removed, `cycle_duration_seconds` added). Three tasks for run-log module wiring, halt-path logging, and acceptance validation.
(b) **References pre-architecture design** — points to README, no verify-flow or Layer 1/2 naming. This is the grading-signal infrastructure (run-log schema).
(c) **Not superseded**; foundational grading artefact that KR measurement depends on.
(d) No staleness; tasks landed with schema amendments documented.

---

**docs/tasks/us-d-cycle-drain-self-grading.md**
(a) The task plan for US-D (cycle drain self-grading), last updated 2026-05-22, defining the `drain-cycle grade` subcommand with 5 tasks for skeleton, per-cycle section, across-cycles trend, verdict bands, and acceptance validation.
(b) **References pre-architecture design** — points to README, no verify-flow or Layer 1/2. This is the grading *command* that consumes the US-C run-log artefacts.
(c) **Not superseded**; implemented alongside US-C to complete the grading loop.
(d) No staleness; tasks planned with open question re-deferred to implementation.

---

**docs/ideas/stacked-pr-finishing.md**
(a) A design idea (no date, but referencing ABA-366 / N08) proposing slice-during-build PR finishing with a recovery-aware skill that commits in reviewable slices and maps them to stacked PRs. Explores Decision Directions A–C, rejects the first two, recommends B.
(b) **References pre-architecture design** — no Layer 1/2 or verify-flow mention; treats PR finishing as an orchestrator concern ("move PR finishing into a skill"). This predates the multi-agent initiative that would subsume it.
(c) **Partially superseded by multi-agent-collaboration.md Tasks 10–13** (PR-shape gate, PR-prepare, PR-respond skills) — but this doc advocates for slice-during-build as a *first* commitment, while the initiative defers the decomposition question and focuses on routing and feedback loop first.
(d) No date; unclear whether implemented or paused. The spike references (ABA-366) suggest it was concurrent planning, not completed.

---

**docs/ideas/drain-past-the-merge-gate.md**
(a) A design vision (no date) proposing a three-gear evolution toward a "resident daemon" that auto-merges trusted PRs and watches for newly-unblocked work. Gear 1 (optimistic stacking), Gear 2 (trust-tiered auto-merge, MVP), Gear 3 (resident daemon). Explicitly defers the daemon and proposes an interim relaunch host.
(b) **References pre-architecture design** — no Layer 1/2; treats PR merging as a single-operator orchestrator concern (auto-merge gating, restack). This is post-US-A/B/C/D visioning but pre-multi-agent-initiative.
(c) **Not superseded by multi-agent-collaboration.md** — that initiative focuses on *execution* quality (verify-flow, grading); this doc focuses on *post-merge* velocity (watching PRs, unblocking downstream). Different concern, non-overlapping.
(d) No date; three gears are speculative; unclear if any were actioned or if this remains a reference design.

---

**docs/adrs/0001-integration-test-architecture.md**
(a) An ADR (Architectural Decision Record), dated 2026-06-02, accepted status. Specifies the testing seam: parent HTTP mock (MockLinear) + Linear-MCP shim + real `claude -p` + in-process harness driver.
(b) **Does not reference Layer 1/2 or verify-flow** — it is a *meta-architectural* decision about testing infrastructure, not product architecture. It enables testing of the orchestrator (Layer 1 orchestration), which is orthogonal to the Layer 1/2 product split.
(c) **Not superseded**; this is the chosen approach. Concurrent with `docs/integration-test-architecture.md` (the full design doc), of which this ADR is the *decision slice*.
(d) No staleness. Clear revisit conditions recorded.

---

**docs/integration-test-architecture.md**
(a) A full design doc, 399 lines, no explicit date but cross-references commit `13d9f70` (2026-05-22 code review) and Linear initiative on integration test architecture. Specifies the system context (three pillars: MockLinear, linear_mcp_shim, IntegrationHarness), workflow, 12 slices, failure-mode coverage matrix, and scenario catalogue.
(b) **Does not reference Layer 1/2 or verify-flow architecture** — it is testing infrastructure design, not product architecture. It enables integration testing of the base orchestrator (US-A–D), which is Layer 1. The multi-agent initiatives (verify-flow, grading) layer on top and will eventually need their own scenario coverage.
(c) **Supersedes the ADR (0001)** — the ADR is the *decision* slice (chosen approach + alternatives); this doc is the *full design* (all context, slices, scenarios). The ADR points to this doc.

# Drain past the merge gate

## Problem Statement
How might we let a drain run keep doing useful work — and keep turning hands-free — when the only thing left blocking it is a human review-and-merge gate on PRs it already opened?

## Context
drain-cycle is transactional per issue: a worker marks a Linear issue **Done**, the orchestrator stacks its PR via Graphite, and continues. Within a run, downstream work stacks fine.
